newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco to resume talks with Sudbury union.
newsitem.headline: Inco to resume talks with Sudbury union.

text.p: Inco Ltd said on Tuesday that it would resume talks on Wednesday with representatives of striking workers at its Sudbury, Ontario nickel mine.

Inco spokesman Jerry Rodgers told Reuters that provincial mediator Dennis Nelson called the two parties together for a meeting and that the nickel miner hoped the dispute could be resolved as early as this weekend.
"We are hopeful this latest meeting will result in a settlement later this week," Rodgers said.

Inco's 4,670 unionized Sudbury workers, represented by the United Steelworkers of America, local 6500, went on strike at midnight on Monday, June 2, after voting 60.4 percent against a contract offer endorsed by union leaders.
According to Inco's 1997 production plan, the Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper and about four million pounds of cobalt.

Inco's Port Colborne, Ontario refinery, which processes cobalt, precious metals and electro-nickel, was not affected by the Sudbury strike. Unionized workers at the refinery approved the contract on Monday, June 2.
